glosses: to zoom, to zoom in
Personne née entre 1997 et 2010 environ, membre de la génération Z.

examples.text: Pour les pourvoir, les grandes maisons du luxe sillonnent les quatre coins de la France à la recherche de « zoomers », l’autre nom de la génération Z.
Des critères éliminatoires pour de nombreux patrons, qui hésitent désormais à embaucher ces zoomers.

glosses: Photographier ou filmer en gros plan en utilisant un zoom.

examples.text: Armer, zoomer, suspendre son souffle, appuyer et recommencer.

glosses: Modifier l’affichage d’une image pour la voir en gros plan.
Regarder quelque chose de plus près, porter son attention sur une partie particulière d’une situation.

examples.text: On zoome un peu plus et on en arrive à Jérusalem, la mère de toutes les discordes au cours des décennies de processus de paix.

glosses: To increase the focal length of a zoom lens in order to obtain a magnified image, or a close-up.

examples.text: The photographer decided to zoom in on the details of the flower.
The camera operator will zoom in on the subject for a close-up shot.

glosses: To manipulate a display (such as a computer screen) so as to make the image larger.

examples.text: You can zoom in on the map to get a better view of the city.

glosses: A video teleconferencing call.

examples.text: Then, later that day, I logged onto a zoom call and my mother and I set up our yoga mats in the living room, as we had been doing a couple of times a week during the pandemic.

glosses: A humming noise from something moving very fast.

examples.text: the zoom of traffic

glosses: A quick ascent.
A big increase.
An augmentation of a view, by varying the focal length of a lens, or digitally.

examples.text: What's the zoom like on your camera?

glosses: To move fast with a humming noise.

examples.text: We zoomed along the highway.
[…] and it was strange sitting in their brand-new comfortable car and hearing them talk of exams as we zoomed smoothly into town.

glosses: To zoom climb.
To move rapidly.
To go up sharply.

examples.text: prices zoomed

glosses: To change the focal length of a zoom lens.
To manipulate a display so as to magnify or shrink it.

examples.text: to zoom in or zoom out

glosses: To check someone out; to investigate someone that one is interested in.

examples.text: "It boggles my mind what kind of mentality is at work there." He pointed to two recent issues of the magazine that featured cover stories were about Whitney Houston and Luther Vandross, two pop music icons whose sexual orientations have been widely speculated on in Black lesbian and gay communities. "It makes you wonder if it's an insult to the intelligence of Essence’s lesbian and gay leadership," Cunningham said. "Who's really zooming whom here?"

glosses: Representing a humming sound

examples.text: Makowsky was playing the Bassgeige. Zoom... zoom-zoom.... The rest of the orchestra would join in presently.

glosses: Suggesting something moving quickly

examples.text: I would dance a few light fantastic steps to show which way the wind lay, and zoom! Like a breeze I was on the piano stool and doing a velocity exercise.

glosses: Suggesting a sudden change, especially an improvement or an increase
To participate in a video teleconferencing call.
To decrease the focal length of a zoom lens in order to obtain a reduced magnification of the image, or a wider-angle view.

examples.text: The director asked to zoom out for a wider shot of the landscape.
The drone's camera began to zoom out as it ascended higher into the sky.

glosses: To manipulate a display (such as a computer screen) so as to make the image smaller and possibly less detailed.

examples.text: You can zoom out on the screen to see the entire document.

glosses: ζουμάρω
